defaults.permitted_development: Across Cornwall, boundary walls, fences and gates are usually permitted development if they stay no higher than 1 metre next to a highway used by vehicles and no higher than 2 metres elsewhere, or if an already-higher boundary is altered without increasing its height. That fallback can disappear where an Article 4 direction or an old planning condition has removed the normal householder right.

rules.height_rules: Across Cornwall, for ordinary houses, most fence and wall questions come back to the same split between the 1 metre highway-side limit and the 2 metre limit elsewhere.
rules.depth_rules: Across Cornwall, means of enclosure are not controlled by an extension-style depth formula. Height, siting and visual effect do the main planning work.
rules.boundary_rules: Across Cornwall, the same boundary treatment can be acceptable in one position and need permission in another once it fronts a road or sits on a prominent corner.
rules.roof_rules: Across Cornwall, ordinary boundary rules do not create a roof allowance. Gate canopies or covered entrance features should be checked separately.
rules.materials_rules: Across Cornwall, national planning rules focus on height and siting rather than a fixed material list, but visible front boundaries should still use finishes that suit the house and street. Heritage areas are more demanding on detail.

restrictions.conservation_area: A fence or wall in a conservation area may need more than a simple height check, especially if demolition of an older boundary is part of the scheme.
restrictions.listed_building: Boundary works to or around a listed building can require listed building consent, especially where historic walls, railings, piers or gates are being altered or removed.
restrictions.article4_notes: Do not rely on the normal 1 metre or 2 metre rule where Article 4 controls or earlier planning conditions remove those householder rights.

rules.depth_rules: Boundary can still need permission because of its position and visual impact even though there is no formal depth limit.
rules.boundary_rules: Front and corner boundaries usually face the tightest control. Rear boundaries are generally less constrained than road-facing ones.
rules.roof_rules: Canopies or roofed gate features need their own planning check.

restrictions.conservation_area: Conservation area status can tighten the position for boundary works, and separate consent may be needed to demolish an existing wall, fence or gate that contributes to the area's character.
restrictions.listed_building: Listed building controls can apply to fences, gates and walls where they form part of the building's curtilage or historic setting.
restrictions.article4_notes: Do not rely on the normal 1 metre or 2 metre rule where Article 4 controls or earlier planning conditions remove those householder rights.
